answer:
**Answer:**

The album *The Houston Kid* was released on **Sugar Hill Records** (the bluegrass/americana label).  
- **Current owner:** **Concord Bicycle Music** (now operating under **Concord**; its parent company is Concord, which became part of BMG Rights Management in 2026).  

*Brief background*  
- Sugar Hill Records was founded in 1978 by Barry Poss and David Freeman. Poss kept ownership until 1998, after which the label was sold to the Welk Music Group.  
- In **2015, Concord Bicycle Music (now known simply as Concord)** acquired Sugar Hill Records, making Concord the current owner of the label that released Rodney Crowell’s *The Houston Kid*.

So the record label that released *The Houston Kid* is owned by Concord (Concord Bicycle Music).

_**The Houston Kid**_ is the 10th album by American [country music] singer [Rodney Crowell]. It was released through [Sugar Hill] "Sugar Hill Records (bluegrass)") in 2001. **Sugar Hill Records** is an American [bluegrass] and [Americana] "Americana (music)")[record label].

It was founded in [Durham, North Carolina], in 1978 by Barry Poss[[1]]#cite_note-Rosenberg2005-1) and [David Freeman] "David Freeman (music historian)"), the owner of [County Records] and [Rebel Records].[[2]]#cite_note-county-2)[[3]]#cite_note-bluegrass_reader-3) Poss acquired full control of Sugar Hill in 1980 and owned the label until 1998, when he sold it to the [Welk Music Group], owner of [Vanguard Records].[[4]]#cite_note-4) Poss stayed on as president, and in 2002 was promoted to chairman. In 2006, Poss won a Lifetime Achievement Award from the [Americana Music Association].[[5]]#cite_note-allbusiness2-5) In 2008, Welk Music Group appointed [EMI] as distributor of its labels including Sugar Hill.[[6]]#cite_note-6) Sugar Hill continued to operate from Durham N.C. until 2007, when Poss moved the label to [Nashville, Tennessee]. In 2015 the label was acquired by [Concord Bicycle Music].[[7]]#cite_note-7)

Among the many notable artists who have released albums on the label are [Nickel Creek], [Doc Watson], [Townes Van Zandt], [Ricky Skaggs], [Guy Clark], [Robert Earl Keen], [Sam Bush] and [Dolly Parton]. One of Parton's albums for Sugar Hill, _[Halos & Horns]_ (2002), included a song called "Sugar Hill", which she wrote as a tribute to the label.

Founder Barry Poss was inducted into the [International Bluegrass Music Hall of Fame] in 2026.[[8]]#cite_note-8)

**Sugar Hill Records** is an American [bluegrass] and [Americana] "Americana (music)")[record label].

It was founded in [Durham, North Carolina], in 1978 by Barry Poss[[1]]#cite_note-Rosenberg2005-1) and [David Freeman] "David Freeman (music historian)"), the owner of [County Records] and [Rebel Records].[[2]]#cite_note-county-2)[[3]]#cite_note-bluegrass_reader-3) Poss acquired full control of Sugar Hill in 1980 and owned the label until 1998, when he sold it to the [Welk Music Group], owner of [Vanguard Records].[[4]]#cite_note-4) Poss stayed on as president, and in 2002 was promoted to chairman. In 2006, Poss won a Lifetime Achievement Award from the [Americana Music Association].[[5]]#cite_note-allbusiness2-5) In 2008, Welk Music Group appointed [EMI] as distributor of its labels including Sugar Hill.[[6]]#cite_note-6) Sugar Hill continued to operate from Durham N.C. until 2007, when Poss moved the label to [Nashville, Tennessee]. In 2015 the label was acquired by [Concord Bicycle Music].[[7]]#cite_note-7)

Among the many notable artists who have released albums on the label are [Nickel Creek], [Doc Watson], [Townes Van Zandt], [Ricky Skaggs], [Guy Clark], [Robert Earl Keen], [Sam Bush] and [Dolly Parton]. One of Parton's albums for Sugar Hill, _[Halos & Horns]_ (2002), included a song called "Sugar Hill", which she wrote as a tribute to the label.

Founder Barry Poss was inducted into the [International Bluegrass Music Hall of Fame] in 2026.[[8]]#cite_note-8)

**Sugar Hill Records** was an American [record label] specializing in [hip hop music]. Founded by [Sylvia Robinson] and her husband Joe Robinson along with Milton Malden in 1979, it was funded by Tony Riviera and [Morris Levy].[[1]]#cite_note-1)[[2]]#cite_note-2) The name is derived from [Sugar Hill, Manhattan], the birthplace of Sylvia Robinson.

Sugar Hill Records played an important role in the development [hip hop music] between the 1970s and 1980s.[[3]]#cite_note-billboardsylvia-3) In addition to producing million-seller hip hop [12-inch vinyl records], the label was also credited for debuting the careers of popular hip hop music acts [The Sugarhill Gang], [The Sequence], [Funky 4 + 1], and [Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five].[[3]]#cite_note-billboardsylvia-3) During the early 1980s, Sugar Hill became one of the top independent labels in America.[[3]]#cite_note-billboardsylvia-3)

Their son, Joey Robinson, Jr., who worked as an executive at the label, helped recruit and assemble [The Sugarhill Gang] along with Sylvia.[[6]]#cite_note-6)[[7]]#cite_note-7) Bass player Doug Wimbish, who worked with Sylvia Robinson at her previous label All Platinum, joined Sugar Hill and form the house band with drummer Keith Le Blanc and guitarist Skip McDonald.[[3]]#cite_note-billboardsylvia-3)

In September 1979, Sugar Hill Records distributed its first record "[Rapper's Delight]", by The Sugarhill Gang, on [12-inch vinyl records].[[8]]#cite_note-auto-8) "Rapper's Delight" was sampled from disco song "[Good Times] "Good Times (Chic song)")" (1979) by American disco group [Chic] "Chic (band)"). Despite Sugar Hill Records' innovative approach to single-only releases, they found it difficult to market 12-inch singles over 7-inch singles due to pricing.[[4]]#cite_note-billboardmag1996-4) The label also found it difficult to gain airplay despite sending the record to various radio stations. The record eventually gained airplay and became widely successful after WESL St. Louis DJ and programmer Jim Gates was convinced by Sylvia to play the record.[[4]]#cite_note-billboardmag1996-4) After the initial first radio play, the radio station's phone line reportedly jammed due to listeners requesting the song.[[4]]#cite_note-billboardmag1996-4) "Rapper's Delight" went on to reportedly sell 14 million copies.[[9]]#cite_note-independent-9)

Following the success of the song, the label sent the Sugarhill Gang to several concert dates. Attending one of these concerts were [Angie B.], Blondy, and Cheryl the Pearl of the group [The Sequence].[[10]]#cite_note-rollingstone-10) The group made their way backstage and met with Sylvia Robinson, where they performed and demoed their own rap songs.[[10]]#cite_note-rollingstone-10) The group was signed as the second music act of Sugar Hill Records.[[11]]#cite_note-11) In December 1979, they released their debut single "[Funk You Up]", which became the first hip hop song by a female act as well as the first original hip hop song to be released without [sampling] "Sampling (music)").[[12]]#cite_note-Greenberg1999-12) The song reportedly sold over half of a million copies.[[10]]#cite_note-rollingstone-10)

**Sugar Hill Records** is an American [bluegrass] and [Americana] "Americana (music)")[record label].

It was founded in [Durham, North Carolina], in 1978 by Barry Poss[[1]]#cite_note-Rosenberg2005-1) and [David Freeman] "David Freeman (music historian)"), the owner of [County Records] and [Rebel Records].[[2]]#cite_note-county-2)[[3]]#cite_note-bluegrass_reader-3) Poss acquired full control of Sugar Hill in 1980 and owned the label until 1998, when he sold it to the [Welk Music Group], owner of [Vanguard Records].[[4]]#cite_note-4) Poss stayed on as president, and in 2002 was promoted to chairman. In 2006, Poss won a Lifetime Achievement Award from the [Americana Music Association].[[5]]#cite_note-allbusiness2-5) In 2008, Welk Music Group appointed [EMI] as distributor of its labels including Sugar Hill.[[6]]#cite_note-6) Sugar Hill continued to operate from Durham N.C. until 2007, when Poss moved the label to [Nashville, Tennessee]. In 2015 the label was acquired by [Concord Bicycle Music].[[7]]#cite_note-7)

Among the many notable artists who have released albums on the label are [Nickel Creek], [Doc Watson], [Townes Van Zandt], [Ricky Skaggs], [Guy Clark], [Robert Earl Keen], [Sam Bush] and [Dolly Parton]. One of Parton's albums for Sugar Hill, _[Halos & Horns]_ (2002), included a song called "Sugar Hill", which she wrote as a tribute to the label.

Founder Barry Poss was inducted into the [International Bluegrass Music Hall of Fame] in 2026.[[8]]#cite_note-8)

steps.reasoning: The question: "Who owns the record label of the performer of The Houston Kid?" Performer: Rodney Crowell. His record label: Sugar Hill Records (bluegrass). Owner is who? According to the article, "Founded in 1978 by Barry Poss and David Freeman. Poss owned until 1998. In 2015 the label was acquired by Concord Bicycle Music." So current owner: Concord Bicycle Music (now part of Concord?) also indicated parent company is Concord (later BMG). So answer: Concord Bicycle Music (Concord). So state: Sugar Hill Records is now owned by Concord (Concord Bicycle Music), formerly owned by Barry Poss. Provide citation.
steps.text:
**Answer:**

The album *The Houston Kid* was released on **Sugar Hill Records** (the bluegrass/americana label).  
- **Current owner:** **Concord Bicycle Music** (now operating under **Concord**; its parent company is Concord, which became part of BMG Rights Management in 2026).  

*Brief background*  
- Sugar Hill Records was founded in 1978 by Barry Poss and David Freeman. Poss kept ownership until 1998, after which the label was sold to the Welk Music Group.  
- In **2015, Concord Bicycle Music (now known simply as Concord)** acquired Sugar Hill Records, making Concord the current owner of the label that released Rodney Crowell’s *The Houston Kid*.

So the record label that released *The Houston Kid* is owned by Concord (Concord Bicycle Music).
